prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Britain forward, not back. New Labour applies enduring Labour values to today’s priorities: government’s duty is to provide opportunity and security for all in a fast‑changing world. Our progressive consensus rejects the false choices of the past: we bind economic dynamism to social justice; investment to reform; individual rights to personal responsibility; and national interest to international engagement.

Record and direction. Since 1997 Britain has enjoyed the longest period of growth in modern times, low inflation and mortgage rates, two million more in work, the Minimum Wage and tax credits making work pay, and fewer children and pensioners in poverty. Crime is down by 30 per cent, police numbers are at a record high, and aid, climate leadership and our influence in Europe have grown. We will build on this: no return to boom and bust or one‑size‑fits‑all services; we go forward to an opportunity economy, personalised public services free at the point of need, and strong, safe communities for those who play by the rules.

Economy and work. We entrench stability with strict fiscal rules, low debt, and no rise in basic or top income tax. We back enterprise, science and skills, raise R&D, modernise regulation, and invest in transport. Our goal is full employment, with active welfare to work, reform of incapacity benefits, higher minimum wage, and regional policies so all can share prosperity. We uphold fair treatment at work and tackle discrimination across gender, race, disability, age, religion and sexuality.

Education. Our aim is personalised learning from early years through 14–19 and higher education: more and better‑supported teachers, sustained funding with multi‑year school budgets, parents as partners, discipline upheld, every secondary an independent specialist school, 200 Academies in deprived areas, strong vocational routes and apprenticeships, and expanded, fairer higher education with fees capped and bursaries for the less well‑off.

Crime, borders and security. We will deliver neighbourhood policing teams everywhere, tough action on antisocial behaviour and alcohol‑fuelled disorder, expand drug testing and treatment, target organised crime through SOCA, and focus on rehabilitation to cut reoffending while ensuring victims’ rights. We support a fair, firm immigration system: a points‑based scheme for skilled migration, stronger borders with biometrics and ID cards, faster, robust asylum decisions, and new counter‑terror powers that protect both liberty and security.

NHS and public health. Investment and reform have cut waits and saved lives; next we guarantee a maximum 18 weeks from referral to treatment, more services closer to home, community hospitals, and patient power and choice across a mixed, NHS‑standard provider base—free, based on need, not ability to pay. We will drive cleaner, safer care and tackle the causes of ill‑health with better school food, smoking restrictions, clear food labelling and targeted action on inequalities.

Families, housing and older people. We will halve child poverty on the way to ending it, expand universal childcare and Sure Start, extend paid maternity/paternity leave and flexible work, and grow homeownership while boosting and modernising social housing. Pension Credit secures today’s pensioners; we will forge a long‑term pensions settlement that is fair, sustainable and rewards saving, support later‑life work, and offer individual care budgets.

Britain in the world. We will keep Britain leading in a reformed EU (with a referendum on the Constitutional Treaty), uphold NATO and our independent nuclear deterrent, support democracy in Iraq and Middle East peace, curb WMD proliferation, reform the UN, and lead on climate change (deep CO2 cuts) and Africa (0.7% aid by 2013, debt relief, fairer trade).

Democracy and communities. We deepen devolution, empower neighbourhoods and local councils, modernise Parliament and complete Lords reform, strengthen civil society and youth volunteering, and advance equality and human rights with a Single Equality Act. Our social contract is clear: we help you to help yourself—so you benefit, and the country benefits.
